harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent, protected sudo command logging on node1. Records include timestamp, invoking user, target user, working directory, and command in /var/log/sudo-commands.log, with no duplicate command entries in system logs or journald. Verified behavior after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Added a validated sudoers fragment using sudo’s native file logging, disabled syslog duplication, disabled line wrapping, and made logging fail closed.
Created root-only logging with SELinux-compatible context and weekly rotation retaining 13 archives.
Verified unprivileged users cannot read the log.
Preserved RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; installed no software.
Restarted node1 safely and verified configuration, prior log data, services, and fresh logging recovered.

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: Direct pre- and post-restart records contain timestamps, invoking user root, target user nobody, working directory, and complete commands.

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries stay out of general system logging
evidence.summary: Unique markers were absent from /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and journald both before and after restart.
Sudoers validation passed; logging is fail-closed and unwrapped; the log is root-owned mode 0600 with var_log_t context; log rotation is configured; unprivileged reads are denied.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel are preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 match before and after the work.

Healthy baseline boot ID 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c was captured; the reboot was safely scheduled and acknowledged; execution returned with changed boot ID d944aa87-2a04-4b12-8581-d73335f567b7; system state, rsyslog, journald, configuration, prior records, access restrictions, and fresh sudo logging all recovered.
